source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue in Brazil covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational breakdowns by state (UF) and municipality.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Brazilian Ministry of Health (MS/SVSA) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos and informes de dengue that are the authoritative primary source for confirmed, probable, suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde – SES) reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Q1 2024 dengue data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

Primary collection source for all target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue in Brazil covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational breakdowns by state (UF) and municipality.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde – SES) reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Q1 2024 dengue data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

Targeting MoH/SVS bulletin terminology ('boletim epidemiológico', 'casos', 'óbitos') with month names for Q1 2024 maximises retrieval of the highest-authority source for all target fields including subnational breakdowns.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde) or SVS weekly epidemiological bulletin (Boletim Epidemiológico) with national and state-level dengue case and death counts for Q1 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: gov.br domain, SVS authorship, official bulletin numbering, SINAN/InfoDengue data citation

iterative_search_queries.query: PAHO WHO dengue Brazil 2024 situation report cases deaths Q1 outbreak
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: PAHO is the primary international body monitoring dengue in the Americas and regularly publishes situation reports with Brazil-specific data. This provides cross-validation of Brazilian MoH figures and may include hospitalization and case-classification breakdowns.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO (Pan American Health Organization) or WHO epidemiological alert, situation report, or regional dengue update covering Brazil Q1 2024 with cumulative case and death counts
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: paho.int or who.int domain, official situation report or epidemiological alert document, dated 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: dengue Brasil 2024 surto casos confirmados mortes estados epidemia primeiro trimestre
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Portuguese-language news sources frequently report subnational (state and municipality) dengue data citing official secretariats, filling gaps in locality and date_reported fields not always visible in national bulletins. The 2024 Q1 dengue season was widely covered in Brazilian media.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Brazilian news outlets (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, UOL) reporting on the 2024 dengue outbreak with state-level or city-level case and death figures, citing official sources
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Named Brazilian news outlet, quotes from Ministério da Saúde or state health secretariats, specific numeric figures with dates

iterative_search_queries.query: dengue Brazil 2024 outbreak cases deaths ProMED HealthMap ECDC surveillance report January March
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: ProMED and HealthMap aggregate and archive outbreak reports with structured metadata and source citations, providing an independent cross-check on case counts and enabling discovery of additional primary source URLs. ECDC may have published a rapid risk assessment given the scale of the 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: ProMED mail archive posts, HealthMap alerts, or ECDC rapid risk assessment referencing Brazil dengue 2024 with quantitative case/death data and source citations
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: ProMED post with archive number, ECDC rapid risk assessment document, HealthMap event ID, dated within Q1 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: dengue Brasil semana epidemiológica 2024 boletim casos óbitos internações janeiro fevereiro março SE1 SE13 situação epidemiológica
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Targets Brazilian MoH/SVS weekly epidemiological bulletins using 'semana epidemiológica' (SE) terminology and the SE1–SE13 range corresponding to Q1 2024 (January–March). Adding 'internações' (hospitalizations) increases the chance of retrieving bulletins that include hospitalization counts. This is the highest-priority gap: Q1-specific national cumulative figures with case classification and hospitalization breakdowns.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Brazilian MoH/SVS Boletim Epidemiológico covering SE1–SE13 of 2024 with national cumulative dengue case counts (confirmed, probable, suspected), deaths, and hospitalizations broken down by epidemiological week and state
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: gov.br domain, SVS authorship, bulletin volume/number referencing SE1–SE13 of 2024, SINAN/InfoDengue data citation
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: q1_001 — iteration 1 retrieved gov.br Boletim vol.55 no.11 referencing SE4/2024 but Q1-complete bulletin with SE1–SE13 data not yet confirmed; adding 'internações' and SE range to improve time-window and field coverage

iterative_search_queries.query: PAHO dengue Brazil epidemiological alert situation report February March 2024 cases deaths outbreak
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Iteration 1 PAHO results were from October 2024, not Q1. PAHO published specific epidemiological alerts for the Brazil dengue outbreak in February–March 2024 given the record-breaking scale. Explicitly targeting February and March 2024 with 'epidemiological alert' terminology should retrieve the Q1-specific PAHO documents that were missed in iteration 1.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO epidemiological alert or situation report published in February or March 2024 specifically addressing the Brazil dengue outbreak with Q1 case and death counts
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: paho.int or who.int domain, document dated February–March 2024, official epidemiological alert format with Brazil-specific quantitative data
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: q1_002 — PAHO results from iteration 1 were October 2024 alerts, not Q1 2024; this query explicitly targets the February–March 2024 period when PAHO would have issued alerts for the Brazil outbreak peak

iterative_search_queries.query: dengue 2024 casos óbitos primeiro trimestre São Paulo Minas Gerais Rio de Janeiro Goiás Distrito Federal secretaria saúde boletim
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Subnational (state-level) Q1 2024 data is a critical gap. The five highest-burden states in 2024 (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, Distrito Federal) each have state health secretariats publishing their own epidemiological bulletins. Targeting all five in a single query with Q1 terminology ('primeiro trimestre') maximises retrieval of state-level case/death breakdowns for the subnational_location and locality fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State health secretariat (Secretaria de Saúde) epidemiological bulletins from São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, or Distrito Federal with Q1 2024 dengue case and death counts at state or municipality level
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: State gov.br subdomains (saude.sp.gov.br, saude.mg.gov.br, saude.rj.gov.br, saude.go.gov.br, saude.df.gov.br), official bulletin authorship, SINAN data citation, dates within Q1 2024

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: ProMED archive post number and date within Q1 2024; ECDC document on ecdc.europa.eu dated Q1 2024; HealthMap event ID with Brazil dengue Q1 2024 data

input.user_request: Collect Dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Brazil from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.

structured_task.user_request: Collect Dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Brazil from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.

collection_spec.data_focus: human Dengue case, outbreak, and surveillance data
collection_spec.user_request: Collect Dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Brazil from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.

surveillance_terms: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação
likely_reporting_agencies: Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA)
count_semantics_notes: Distinguish confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts; Brazilian dengue reporting commonly uses 'casos prováveis' as the primary surveillance count, which includes confirmed and probable.
Separate locally acquired (autóctones) from travel-associated (importados) cases.
Dengue reports in Brazil use epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); map SE to calendar dates for the 2024-Q1 window (SE01–SE13).
Cumulative counts may be reported year-to-date; extract period-specific counts where possible and flag if cumulative.
Deaths may be reported as confirmed or under investigation (em investigação); note classification status.
Brazil experienced a major dengue epidemic in early 2024; case volumes may be very high and reports may use aggregated national totals alongside state-level breakdowns.
SINAN data may lag real-time reporting; boletins epidemiológicos may reflect data up to a specific closing date.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue counts with aggregate arbovirus counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly reported.
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito surveillance or vector control metrics as human case counts.
Do not conflate 'casos prováveis' (probable, the Brazilian surveillance standard) with 'confirmed' in the strict laboratory-confirmed sense without noting the distinction.
Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; verify whether figures are national totals, state-level, or municipal-level before recording subnational_location.
Multiple serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4) may be co-circulating; serotype data is supplementary and should not be confused with case classification.
Distinguish between 'dengue grave' (severe dengue) and 'dengue com sinais de alarme' (dengue with warning signs) — these are clinical severity categories, not separate diseases.
News reports may cite preliminary or unofficial figures; always prefer official boletins for case counts.
suggested_query_terms: dengue surveillance Brazil January February March 2024

Field mappings (especially for case classification tiers) must reflect Dengue semantics.

EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Brazil declared a public health emergency for dengue in February 2024; case volumes for Q1 2024 are exceptionally high. Collectors should expect large cumulative figures and frequent situation report updates.
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — Multiple DENV serotypes (especially DENV-3 reemergence alongside DENV-1) were reported in Brazil in early 2024; serotype data is supplementary but may appear in official reports.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources will be in Brazilian Portuguese. Query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').

GEOGRAPHIC GRANULARITY — Brazil has 26 states + 1 federal district and 5,570 municipalities. Subnational_location should capture state (UF) at minimum; locality should capture municipality where reported. Do not aggregate state figures into national totals without flagging.
TIME GRANULARITY — Q1 2024 corresponds to Epidemiological Weeks SE01–SE13 (approximately January 1 – March 30, 2024). Map SE numbers to calendar date ranges when populating date_reported.
DATA LAG — SINAN-based official counts may be subject to reporting delays of 1–4 weeks; boletim closing dates should be recorded in evidence_quote or notes.

CASE CLASSIFICATION — Brazilian dengue surveillance classifies cases as: (1) dengue sem sinais de alarme, (2) dengue com sinais de alarme, (3) dengue grave. Map these to cases_confirmed / cases_probable / cases_suspected fields with a classification note.

DO NOT INVENT URLs — This profile provides source planning intelligence only. No URLs have been discovered or validated. Source URLs must be obtained through actual source discovery and collection steps.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue in Brazil covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational breakdowns by state (UF) and municipality.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Brazilian Ministry of Health (MS/SVSA) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos and informes de dengue that are the authoritative primary source for confirmed, probable, suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde – SES) reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Q1 2024 dengue data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde do Brasil / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA) publishes authoritative weekly boletins epidemiológicos de dengue and informes de arboviroses covering national and state-level case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and epidemiological week data. Primary collection source for all target fields.

State health secretariats (SES) of high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Rio Grande do Sul) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with municipal-level breakdowns, enabling subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas with Brazil-specific case and death counts, epidemiological week breakdowns, and serotype data. Serves as both collection and validation source.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue totals for Brazil that can validate extracted records from primary sources.

Structured surveillance databases including InfoDengue (Fiocruz), SINAN open data (DATASUS), and Brasil.io provide queryable dengue case data at state and municipal levels for Q1 2024, enabling systematic validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype distribution, outbreak dynamics, and epidemiological context for accurate extraction and normalization.

Reputable Brazilian and international news outlets (G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Reuters, ProMED) and situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, and emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts; Brazilian dengue reporting commonly uses 'casos prováveis' as the primary surveillance count, which includes confirmed and probable.
Separate locally acquired (autóctones) from travel-associated (importados) cases.
Dengue reports in Brazil use epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); map SE to calendar dates for the 2024-Q1 window (SE01–SE13).
Cumulative counts may be reported year-to-date; extract period-specific counts where possible and flag if cumulative.
Deaths may be reported as confirmed or under investigation (em investigação); note classification status.
Brazil experienced a major dengue epidemic in early 2024; case volumes may be very high and reports may use aggregated national totals alongside state-level breakdowns.
SINAN data may lag real-time reporting; boletins epidemiológicos may reflect data up to a specific closing date.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue counts with aggregate arbovirus counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly reported.
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito surveillance or vector control metrics as human case counts.
Do not conflate 'casos prováveis' (probable, the Brazilian surveillance standard) with 'confirmed' in the strict laboratory-confirmed sense without noting the distinction.
Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; verify whether figures are national totals, state-level, or municipal-level before recording subnational_location.
Multiple serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4) may be co-circulating; serotype data is supplementary and should not be confused with case classification.
Distinguish between 'dengue grave' (severe dengue) and 'dengue com sinais de alarme' (dengue with warning signs) — these are clinical severity categories, not separate diseases.
News reports may cite preliminary or unofficial figures; always prefer official boletins for case counts.

EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Brazil declared a public health emergency for dengue in February 2024; case volumes for Q1 2024 are exceptionally high. Collectors should expect large cumulative figures and frequent situation report updates.
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — Multiple DENV serotypes (especially DENV-3 reemergence alongside DENV-1) were reported in Brazil in early 2024; serotype data is supplementary but may appear in official reports.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources will be in Brazilian Portuguese. Query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').

GEOGRAPHIC GRANULARITY — Brazil has 26 states + 1 federal district and 5,570 municipalities. Subnational_location should capture state (UF) at minimum; locality should capture municipality where reported. Do not aggregate state figures into national totals without flagging.
TIME GRANULARITY — Q1 2024 corresponds to Epidemiological Weeks SE01–SE13 (approximately January 1 – March 30, 2024). Map SE numbers to calendar date ranges when populating date_reported.
DATA LAG — SINAN-based official counts may be subject to reporting delays of 1–4 weeks; boletim closing dates should be recorded in evidence_quote or notes.

CASE CLASSIFICATION — Brazilian dengue surveillance classifies cases as: (1) dengue sem sinais de alarme, (2) dengue com sinais de alarme, (3) dengue grave. Map these to cases_confirmed / cases_probable / cases_suspected fields with a classification note.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts; Brazilian dengue reporting commonly uses 'casos prováveis' as the primary surveillance count, which includes confirmed and probable.
Separate locally acquired (autóctones) from travel-associated (importados) cases.
Dengue reports in Brazil use epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); map SE to calendar dates for the 2024-Q1 window (SE01–SE13).
Cumulative counts may be reported year-to-date; extract period-specific counts where possible and flag if cumulative.
Deaths may be reported as confirmed or under investigation (em investigação); note classification status.
Brazil experienced a major dengue epidemic in early 2024; case volumes may be very high and reports may use aggregated national totals alongside state-level breakdowns.
SINAN data may lag real-time reporting; boletins epidemiológicos may reflect data up to a specific closing date.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue counts with aggregate arbovirus counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly reported.
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito surveillance or vector control metrics as human case counts.
Do not conflate 'casos prováveis' (probable, the Brazilian surveillance standard) with 'confirmed' in the strict laboratory-confirmed sense without noting the distinction.
Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; verify whether figures are national totals, state-level, or municipal-level before recording subnational_location.
Multiple serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4) may be co-circulating; serotype data is supplementary and should not be confused with case classification.
Distinguish between 'dengue grave' (severe dengue) and 'dengue com sinais de alarme' (dengue with warning signs) — these are clinical severity categories, not separate diseases.
News reports may cite preliminary or unofficial figures; always prefer official boletins for case counts.

EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Brazil declared a public health emergency for dengue in February 2024; case volumes for Q1 2024 are exceptionally high. Collectors should expect large cumulative figures and frequent situation report updates.
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — Multiple DENV serotypes (especially DENV-3 reemergence alongside DENV-1) were reported in Brazil in early 2024; serotype data is supplementary but may appear in official reports.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources will be in Brazilian Portuguese. Query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').

GEOGRAPHIC GRANULARITY — Brazil has 26 states + 1 federal district and 5,570 municipalities. Subnational_location should capture state (UF) at minimum; locality should capture municipality where reported. Do not aggregate state figures into national totals without flagging.
TIME GRANULARITY — Q1 2024 corresponds to Epidemiological Weeks SE01–SE13 (approximately January 1 – March 30, 2024). Map SE numbers to calendar date ranges when populating date_reported.
DATA LAG — SINAN-based official counts may be subject to reporting delays of 1–4 weeks; boletim closing dates should be recorded in evidence_quote or notes.

CASE CLASSIFICATION — Brazilian dengue surveillance classifies cases as: (1) dengue sem sinais de alarme, (2) dengue com sinais de alarme, (3) dengue grave. Map these to cases_confirmed / cases_probable / cases_suspected fields with a classification note.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Brazilian Ministry of Health (MS/SVSA) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos and informes de dengue that are the authoritative primary source for confirmed, probable, suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

collection_spec.user_request: Collect Dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Brazil from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.

surveillance_terms: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação
likely_reporting_agencies: Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA)
count_semantics_notes: Distinguish confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts; Brazilian dengue reporting commonly uses 'casos prováveis' as the primary surveillance count, which includes confirmed and probable.
Separate locally acquired (autóctones) from travel-associated (importados) cases.
Dengue reports in Brazil use epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); map SE to calendar dates for the 2024-Q1 window (SE01–SE13).
Cumulative counts may be reported year-to-date; extract period-specific counts where possible and flag if cumulative.
Deaths may be reported as confirmed or under investigation (em investigação); note classification status.
Brazil experienced a major dengue epidemic in early 2024; case volumes may be very high and reports may use aggregated national totals alongside state-level breakdowns.
SINAN data may lag real-time reporting; boletins epidemiológicos may reflect data up to a specific closing date.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue counts with aggregate arbovirus counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly reported.
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito surveillance or vector control metrics as human case counts.
Do not conflate 'casos prováveis' (probable, the Brazilian surveillance standard) with 'confirmed' in the strict laboratory-confirmed sense without noting the distinction.
Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; verify whether figures are national totals, state-level, or municipal-level before recording subnational_location.
Multiple serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4) may be co-circulating; serotype data is supplementary and should not be confused with case classification.
Distinguish between 'dengue grave' (severe dengue) and 'dengue com sinais de alarme' (dengue with warning signs) — these are clinical severity categories, not separate diseases.
News reports may cite preliminary or unofficial figures; always prefer official boletins for case counts.

EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Brazil declared a public health emergency for dengue in February 2024; case volumes for Q1 2024 are exceptionally high. Collectors should expect large cumulative figures and frequent situation report updates.
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — Multiple DENV serotypes (especially DENV-3 reemergence alongside DENV-1) were reported in Brazil in early 2024; serotype data is supplementary but may appear in official reports.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources will be in Brazilian Portuguese. Query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').

GEOGRAPHIC GRANULARITY — Brazil has 26 states + 1 federal district and 5,570 municipalities. Subnational_location should capture state (UF) at minimum; locality should capture municipality where reported. Do not aggregate state figures into national totals without flagging.
TIME GRANULARITY — Q1 2024 corresponds to Epidemiological Weeks SE01–SE13 (approximately January 1 – March 30, 2024). Map SE numbers to calendar date ranges when populating date_reported.
DATA LAG — SINAN-based official counts may be subject to reporting delays of 1–4 weeks; boletim closing dates should be recorded in evidence_quote or notes.

CASE CLASSIFICATION — Brazilian dengue surveillance classifies cases as: (1) dengue sem sinais de alarme, (2) dengue com sinais de alarme, (3) dengue grave. Map these to cases_confirmed / cases_probable / cases_suspected fields with a classification note.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue in Brazil covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational breakdowns by state (UF) and municipality.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Brazilian Ministry of Health (MS/SVSA) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos and informes de dengue that are the authoritative primary source for confirmed, probable, suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde – SES) reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Q1 2024 dengue data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde do Brasil / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA) publishes authoritative weekly boletins epidemiológicos de dengue and informes de arboviroses covering national and state-level case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and epidemiological week data. Primary collection source for all target fields.

State health secretariats (SES) of high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Rio Grande do Sul) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with municipal-level breakdowns, enabling subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas with Brazil-specific case and death counts, epidemiological week breakdowns, and serotype data. Serves as both collection and validation source.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue totals for Brazil that can validate extracted records from primary sources.

Structured surveillance databases including InfoDengue (Fiocruz), SINAN open data (DATASUS), and Brasil.io provide queryable dengue case data at state and municipal levels for Q1 2024, enabling systematic validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype distribution, outbreak dynamics, and epidemiological context for accurate extraction and normalization.

Reputable Brazilian and international news outlets (G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Reuters, ProMED) and situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, and emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts.

Jornalismo TV Cultura

O aumento de 400% nos óbitos devido aos casos de dengue acendeu a luz vermelha no Governo Federal, estados e prefeituras.

surveillance_terms: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação
likely_reporting_agencies: Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA)
count_semantics_notes: Distinguish confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts; Brazilian dengue reporting commonly uses 'casos prováveis' as the primary surveillance count, which includes confirmed and probable.
Separate locally acquired (autóctones) from travel-associated (importados) cases.
Dengue reports in Brazil use epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); map SE to calendar dates for the 2024-Q1 window (SE01–SE13).
Cumulative counts may be reported year-to-date; extract period-specific counts where possible and flag if cumulative.
Deaths may be reported as confirmed or under investigation (em investigação); note classification status.
Brazil experienced a major dengue epidemic in early 2024; case volumes may be very high and reports may use aggregated national totals alongside state-level breakdowns.
SINAN data may lag real-time reporting; boletins epidemiológicos may reflect data up to a specific closing date.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue counts with aggregate arbovirus counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly reported.
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito surveillance or vector control metrics as human case counts.
Do not conflate 'casos prováveis' (probable, the Brazilian surveillance standard) with 'confirmed' in the strict laboratory-confirmed sense without noting the distinction.
Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; verify whether figures are national totals, state-level, or municipal-level before recording subnational_location.
Multiple serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4) may be co-circulating; serotype data is supplementary and should not be confused with case classification.
Distinguish between 'dengue grave' (severe dengue) and 'dengue com sinais de alarme' (dengue with warning signs) — these are clinical severity categories, not separate diseases.
News reports may cite preliminary or unofficial figures; always prefer official boletins for case counts.

EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Brazil declared a public health emergency for dengue in February 2024; case volumes for Q1 2024 are exceptionally high. Collectors should expect large cumulative figures and frequent situation report updates.
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — Multiple DENV serotypes (especially DENV-3 reemergence alongside DENV-1) were reported in Brazil in early 2024; serotype data is supplementary but may appear in official reports.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources will be in Brazilian Portuguese. Query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').

GEOGRAPHIC GRANULARITY — Brazil has 26 states + 1 federal district and 5,570 municipalities. Subnational_location should capture state (UF) at minimum; locality should capture municipality where reported. Do not aggregate state figures into national totals without flagging.
TIME GRANULARITY — Q1 2024 corresponds to Epidemiological Weeks SE01–SE13 (approximately January 1 – March 30, 2024). Map SE numbers to calendar date ranges when populating date_reported.
DATA LAG — SINAN-based official counts may be subject to reporting delays of 1–4 weeks; boletim closing dates should be recorded in evidence_quote or notes.

CASE CLASSIFICATION — Brazilian dengue surveillance classifies cases as: (1) dengue sem sinais de alarme, (2) dengue com sinais de alarme, (3) dengue grave. Map these to cases_confirmed / cases_probable / cases_suspected fields with a classification note.

DO NOT INVENT URLs — This profile provides source planning intelligence only. No URLs have been discovered or validated. Source URLs must be obtained through actual source discovery and collection steps.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue in Brazil covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational breakdowns by state (UF) and municipality.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Brazilian Ministry of Health (MS/SVSA) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos and informes de dengue that are the authoritative primary source for confirmed, probable, suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde – SES) reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Q1 2024 dengue data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde do Brasil / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA) publishes authoritative weekly boletins epidemiológicos de dengue and informes de arboviroses covering national and state-level case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and epidemiological week data. Primary collection source for all target fields.

State health secretariats (SES) of high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Rio Grande do Sul) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with municipal-level breakdowns, enabling subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas with Brazil-specific case and death counts, epidemiological week breakdowns, and serotype data. Serves as both collection and validation source.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue totals for Brazil that can validate extracted records from primary sources.

Structured surveillance databases including InfoDengue (Fiocruz), SINAN open data (DATASUS), and Brasil.io provide queryable dengue case data at state and municipal levels for Q1 2024, enabling systematic validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype distribution, outbreak dynamics, and epidemiological context for accurate extraction and normalization.

Reputable Brazilian and international news outlets (G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Reuters, ProMED) and situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, and emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts.

count_semantics_notes: Distinguish confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts; Brazilian dengue reporting commonly uses 'casos prováveis' as the primary surveillance count, which includes confirmed and probable.
Separate locally acquired (autóctones) from travel-associated (importados) cases.
Dengue reports in Brazil use epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); map SE to calendar dates for the 2024-Q1 window (SE01–SE13).
Cumulative counts may be reported year-to-date; extract period-specific counts where possible and flag if cumulative.
Deaths may be reported as confirmed or under investigation (em investigação); note classification status.
Brazil experienced a major dengue epidemic in early 2024; case volumes may be very high and reports may use aggregated national totals alongside state-level breakdowns.
SINAN data may lag real-time reporting; boletins epidemiológicos may reflect data up to a specific closing date.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue counts with aggregate arbovirus counts (which may include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly reported.
Do not treat Aedes aegypti mosquito surveillance or vector control metrics as human case counts.
Do not conflate 'casos prováveis' (probable, the Brazilian surveillance standard) with 'confirmed' in the strict laboratory-confirmed sense without noting the distinction.
Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; verify whether figures are national totals, state-level, or municipal-level before recording subnational_location.
Multiple serotypes (DENV-1 through DENV-4) may be co-circulating; serotype data is supplementary and should not be confused with case classification.
Distinguish between 'dengue grave' (severe dengue) and 'dengue com sinais de alarme' (dengue with warning signs) — these are clinical severity categories, not separate diseases.
News reports may cite preliminary or unofficial figures; always prefer official boletins for case counts.

EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Brazil declared a public health emergency for dengue in February 2024; case volumes for Q1 2024 are exceptionally high. Collectors should expect large cumulative figures and frequent situation report updates.
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — Multiple DENV serotypes (especially DENV-3 reemergence alongside DENV-1) were reported in Brazil in early 2024; serotype data is supplementary but may appear in official reports.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources will be in Brazilian Portuguese. Query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').

GEOGRAPHIC GRANULARITY — Brazil has 26 states + 1 federal district and 5,570 municipalities. Subnational_location should capture state (UF) at minimum; locality should capture municipality where reported. Do not aggregate state figures into national totals without flagging.
TIME GRANULARITY — Q1 2024 corresponds to Epidemiological Weeks SE01–SE13 (approximately January 1 – March 30, 2024). Map SE numbers to calendar date ranges when populating date_reported.
DATA LAG — SINAN-based official counts may be subject to reporting delays of 1–4 weeks; boletim closing dates should be recorded in evidence_quote or notes.

CASE CLASSIFICATION — Brazilian dengue surveillance classifies cases as: (1) dengue sem sinais de alarme, (2) dengue com sinais de alarme, (3) dengue grave. Map these to cases_confirmed / cases_probable / cases_suspected fields with a classification note.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) epidemiological bulletins and situation reports for Dengue in Brazil covering 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31, with subnational breakdowns by state (UF) and municipality.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The Brazilian Ministry of Health (MS/SVSA) publishes weekly and periodic boletins epidemiológicos and informes de dengue that are the authoritative primary source for confirmed, probable, suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health secretariat (Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde – SES) reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Q1 2024 dengue data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde do Brasil / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA) publishes authoritative weekly boletins epidemiológicos de dengue and informes de arboviroses covering national and state-level case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and epidemiological week data. Primary collection source for all target fields.

State health secretariats (SES) of high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Rio Grande do Sul) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with municipal-level breakdowns, enabling subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas with Brazil-specific case and death counts, epidemiological week breakdowns, and serotype data. Serves as both collection and validation source.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue totals for Brazil that can validate extracted records from primary sources.

Structured surveillance databases including InfoDengue (Fiocruz), SINAN open data (DATASUS), and Brasil.io provide queryable dengue case data at state and municipal levels for Q1 2024, enabling systematic validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype distribution, outbreak dynamics, and epidemiological context for accurate extraction and normalization.

Reputable Brazilian and international news outlets (G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Reuters, ProMED) and situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, and emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SES reports provide subnational and municipal-level granularity not always available in national bulletins, and are critical for locality-level fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with epidemiological week breakdowns useful for date alignment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., InfoDengue, SINAN open data, Brasil.io, DATASUS) containing dengue surveillance data for Brazil in Q1 2024 for cross-validation of collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently queryable case counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins to detect discrepancies in count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) or geographic scope.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) or ECDC rapid risk assessments referencing the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic for independent validation of national-level totals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DONs and ECDC assessments aggregate data from multiple official sources and serve as independent validation anchors for national case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify sources explaining Brazilian dengue case definitions (dengue sem sinais de alarme, dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave), classification criteria, and reporting methodology used in 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding case classification is essential for correctly mapping extracted counts to schema fields (cases_confirmed, cases_probable, cases_suspected) and interpreting evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic epidemiology, serotype distribution (DENV-1/2/3/4), and outbreak dynamics for contextual interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide methodological context, case definition clarifications, and serotype data that support accurate extraction and normalization of surveillance records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (Reuters, AP, BBC, G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, ProMED) covering the Brazil 2024 dengue outbreak with specific case/death figures and subnational locations.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, or emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts not yet reflected in official bulletins.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly vs. newly reported), unclear geographic scope, or potential validation leakage for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated very high case volumes; sources may mix cumulative annual totals with weekly increments, requiring human judgment on count type assignment.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde do Brasil / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde e Ambiente (SVSA) publishes authoritative weekly boletins epidemiológicos de dengue and informes de arboviroses covering national and state-level case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and epidemiological week data. Primary collection source for all target fields.

State health secretariats (SES) of high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Rio Grande do Sul) publish state-specific dengue bulletins with municipal-level breakdowns, enabling subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes dengue situation reports for the Americas with Brazil-specific case and death counts, epidemiological week breakdowns, and serotype data. Serves as both collection and validation source.
WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue totals for Brazil that can validate extracted records from primary sources.

Structured surveillance databases including InfoDengue (Fiocruz), SINAN open data (DATASUS), and Brasil.io provide queryable dengue case data at state and municipal levels for Q1 2024, enabling systematic validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the 2024 Brazil dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype distribution, outbreak dynamics, and epidemiological context for accurate extraction and normalization.

Reputable Brazilian and international news outlets (G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Reuters, ProMED) and situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, municipal-level data, and emergency declarations with extractable numeric counts.
